validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed, independent of GEM. (1) citizenmatters.in, a Bengaluru investigative-journalism outlet, published a detailed 2018 piece on a real gas leak on this pipeline's Bangalore city-gas distribution network, describing the exact engineering: 'The Dabhol-Bangalore Piped Natural Gas (PNG) runs through two states of Maharashtra and Karnataka for about 1,386 km', an 18-inch steel transmission main at 19 bar reducing to 4 bar through MDP distribution pipe and 21 millibar at the burner tip -- this is physical operational evidence, not just an announcement. (2) The Economic Times (verified live, url_verifier OK) headlined 'PM dedicates GAIL India Ltd's 1,000 km Dabhol-Bangalore gas pipeline to nation', Dec 3, 2013. (3) GAIL's own press release (original gail.nic.in URL is dead -- ConnectionError -- but its Dec-2013 capture on the Wayback Machine is live and verified) confirms: 'Hon'ble Prime Minister ... dedicated to the Nation GAIL (India) Limited's 1,000 km-long natural gas pipeline from Dabhol in Maharashtra to Bangaluru in Karnataka' on Dec 3 2013, 'constructed at an investment of Rs 4,500 crores with a design capacity of 16 MMSCMD', passing through Belgaum, Dharwad, Gadag, Bellary, Devanagere, Chitradurga, Tumkur, Ramanagaram, Bengaluru Rural and Bengaluru Urban -- an exact match to GEM's route. (4) PNGRB's current (May 2026) NGPL MIS report line-wise table lists it as entity GAIL, states MH, KA & GA. Three fully independent origins (an investigative news outlet, a national business daily, and the regulator) plus GAIL's own first-party record -- existence is not in doubt. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct -- citizenmatters explicitly describes the 18in line as the high-pressure transmission main feeding downstream city-gas distribution, consistent with GEM's classification; no evidence of a gathering/feeder misclassification. DUPLICATE: checked against the 35-row India-gas-operating roster. P0930 (Jaigarh-Dabhol Gas Pipeline) shares the 'Dabhol' endpoint but is a distinct, much shorter (60 km) LNG-terminal feeder line commissioned 2021 (Jaigarh LNG Terminal -> Dabhol) that feeds INTO this trunk rather than duplicating it -- not the same physical pipe. No other roster row plausibly overlaps. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% is unanimous across every source found -- GAIL's own release, Economic Times ('GAIL India Ltd's ... pipeline'), and PNGRB (entity=GAIL) all agree; StartYear1=2013 matches the Dec 3, 2013 dedication date in both the GAIL release and Economic Times exactly; Capacity=16.00 MMSCMD matches GAIL's own 'design capacity of 16 MMSCMD' and PNGRB's authorised+design/determined capacity of 16.0 MMSCMD exactly. See the companion spec-concern entry for a length/completion-status caveat that does NOT undermine any of the above.

If it is confirmed dead/abandoned, consider splitting this row the way GEM already splits Mehsana-Bhatinda, Bhatinda-Gurdaspur, Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur, and Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-Mangalore: an `operating` row near PNGRB's current operating length (~1,182 km) plus a `construction`/`shelved` companion row for the unbuilt remainder (~232 km), rather than one `operating` row claiming the full corridor. validity.researcher_notes: PNGRB's own current line-wise register -- the May 2026 'NGPL MIS Report' (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, page 2, fetched and read locally with pdftotext -layout; url_verifier returns a false-negative HTTP 200/'value not found' on this large PDF per the known limitation, so I confirmed the numbers by hand) lists 'Dabhol-Bangalore' (entity GAIL, authorisation date 14.11.2011) under the PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE section, NOT under Operational: Authorised Length 1,414 km, Authorised/Design Capacity 16.0 MMSCMD (matches GEM's Capacity exactly), Operating Length 1,182 km, Under-Construction Length 232 km, and zero lowered/welded/hydrotested length recorded against that 232 km residual, with a 'Target date of completion' of Feb-13 (i.e. February 2013) that lapsed more than thirteen years before this report -- meaning the regulator's own figures show zero measurable progress on the remaining ~232 km for over a decade, i.e. it reads as stalled/dead rather than actively under construction. This conflicts with GEM's row, which shows a SINGLE fully `operating` segment at LengthKnown=1,386 km (no companion under-construction row exists for P0915 in the wider GGIT gas CSV -- confirmed by grep against the full snapshot). 1,386 km is itself well corroborated -- citizenmatters.in (independent, 2018) states the identical figure ('for about 1,386 km'), so GEM's number is not invented -- but it doesn't equal any of PNGRB's own figures (not the 1,414 km authorised total, not the 1,182 km PNGRB currently calls 'operating'); it sits in between. A plausible explanation surfaced from the sheet's own gem.wiki citation list: Wikipedia (read for leads only, not cited) notes the pipeline's original scope 'also extends to Vasco da Gama, Goa', and one of the wiki page's OWN cited references is a Nov 2010 Outlook India piece titled 'Goa: Farmers Oppose Underground Gas Pipeline' -- i.e. a Goa spur ran into land-acquisition opposition around 2010. That Outlook URL now 410s (confirmed dead, cannot cite per the never-delete-but-can't-cite-a-404/410 rule) so this is not proposed as a citable ref, but it is consistent with PNGRB's residual 232 km being the stalled/abandoned Goa extension while the Maharashtra-Karnataka trunk (the part everyone agrees was completed and dedicated in Dec 2013) is fully operating. Net effect: existence/ownership/classification/start-year/capacity are solid (see prior validity entry); it is specifically the completeness of the authorised corridor -- and therefore whether `Status=operating` should cover 100% of a 1,386 km line or should be split -- that is unresolved.
